brief.headline: The eight-session aluminium rally broke: the official cash settlement fell $65.50 (-1.94%) on 12-August, its largest one-day fall of the advance, arriving one session after the price met a widely-watched technical objective almost exactly. The detail that matters more than the size of the fall is that the shape of the curve did not change at all - cash and the three-month dropped by the identical amount - while exchange inventories drew for a 31st straight day, so nothing about the physical availability of prompt metal actually shifted.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. LME official cash aluminium settled $3,307.50 on 12-August, down $65.50 (-1.94%) from $3,373.00, and the three-month settled $3,308.50, down the same $65.50. It is the biggest single-session decline since the rally began in late July and it ends a sequence of five new cycle highs in eight sessions. The move should still be kept in proportion: cash remains $111.50 (+3.49%) above the 31-July level and $148.00 (+4.68%) above the 28-July low. Momentum broke; the trend did not.

WHY THE SHAPE OF THE CURVE IS THE REAL INFORMATION. Because both legs fell by exactly the same $65.50, the cash-to-three-month spread is unchanged at a $1.00 contango - a perfectly parallel downward shift of the front of the curve. That is what position liquidation looks like. A genuine change in prompt physical need, in either direction, moves one leg more than the other; this moved neither relative to the other. For a week the pattern was the reverse - price making new highs while the front end kept surrendering its premium - and both patterns support the same conclusion: the price is being set by expectations and positioning, not by anyone's immediate requirement for metal.

THE INVENTORY SIGNAL WENT THE OTHER WAY, AGAIN. Exchange stocks fell another 1,700 tonnes to 251,700 tonnes, a 31st consecutive daily draw and a fresh low, and the draw rate actually picked up from the 1,500 tonnes a day that had run for most of the prior week. Visible inventory has fallen more than 8% in fifteen sessions and roughly half since January. Prices fell nearly 2% on a day when the metal available on warrant got scarcer - a divergence worth watching rather than explaining away, because it can only persist for so long before one side gives.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. First, whether aluminium's isolation persists: it was the only metal on the base complex to fall meaningfully, while zinc, lead and nickel all rose and a soft US inflation print supported risk assets generally - which argues the move was metal-specific rather than macro. Second, today's ring: a second consecutive down day accompanied by a WIDENING contango would be the first real evidence that the physical market is loosening rather than just the financial one. Third, upstream: the largest alumina refinery outside China is entering a second day at half rate on a gas-supply failure, with the operator publicly guiding a US$75-100 million quarterly impact and giving no restart date - that is a cost risk that builds slowly and does not show up in a daily price.

kpis.note: 12-Aug OFFICIAL $3,307.50 against the 11-August official of $3,373.00 = -$65.50 (-1.94%). THIS IS THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION DECLINE OF THE ENTIRE AUGUST ADVANCE and it ends a run of five new cycle highs in eight sessions. IT ARRIVED EXACTLY ONE SESSION AFTER THE PUBLISHED WAVE TARGET WAS MET. This page has carried a wave-(v) equality objective of $3,373 for a week; the 11-August official printed $3,374.00, met it to within $1.00, and the next session gave back $65.50. Target met, then reversal, is the most common way an impulse ends - it does not prove the count, but it is the sequence the count predicted. KEEP THE MOVE IN PROPORTION, BOTH WAYS. The rally is dented, not broken: cash is still $111.50 (+3.49%) above the 31-July official of $3,196.00 and $148.00 (+4.68%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50. What broke is momentum, not the trend. WHAT DID NOT HAPPEN IS THE INFORMATIVE PART: the curve did not crack. Cash and the 3-month fell by EXACTLY the same $65.50, so this was a perfectly PARALLEL shift of the whole front of the curve and the cash-3M spread is unchanged at a $1.00 contango. A parallel repricing is the signature of length leaving, not of physical stress. And on the same day, stock drew another 1,700 t to a fresh low. Price fell nearly 2% while the metal available on warrant tightened - the exact mirror image of last week, when price rose while the curve loosened. Both configurations point at the same conclusion: prompt physical availability is not what is setting this price. Westmetall LME officials, 12-Aug-2026 session. kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: 12-Aug 3-MONTH OFFICIAL $3,308.50 against $3,374.00 = -$65.50 (-1.94%), the identical dollar move to cash. THE EQUALITY OF THE TWO MOVES IS THE POINT AND IT DESERVES TO BE STATED PLAINLY: for the front of the curve to fall in a perfectly parallel shift, the selling has to be spread evenly across the near tenors rather than concentrated at the prompt date. That is what position liquidation looks like. It is NOT what a physical demand shock looks like, and it is not what a squeeze unwinding looks like either - both of those move one leg more than the other. The 1.618x extension objective at $3,392 was never reached; the high stands at $3,374.00. SECONDARY, DIFFERENT-BASIS REFERENCE FOR THE SAME DAY, QUOTED ONLY AS CORROBORATION AND NOT MIXED INTO THIS ROW: Trading Economics' independent CFD series marks $3,306.75 for 12-August, down 1.60% on a prior mark of $3,360.55, and still +4.79% on the month and +26.66% year-on-year. An independent series agreeing on both the direction and roughly the magnitude of a 2% down day is the corroboration that matters most on a reversal session. avg = the JULY-2026 3-month official monthly mean of $3,149.50 computed across the same 23 published July sessions.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: UNCHANGED AT A $1.00 CONTANGO, AND ON A DAY LIKE TODAY 'UNCHANGED' IS THE HEADLINE. Cash $3,307.50 sits $1.00 BELOW 3-month $3,308.50, precisely as it did yesterday, because both legs fell by exactly $65.50. CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS AGAIN, BUT THE OTHER WAY ROUND FROM YESTERDAY - flat price fell hard while the spread held completely still. That is a materially different message from the one this desk has been flagging all week. When flat price was making new highs, the front end kept surrendering its premium, which said the buying was forward-dated rather than prompt. Now flat price has fallen 1.94% and the front end has NOT loosened further, which says the selling was not prompt either. THE AUGUST SEQUENCE NOW READS: +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 contango, +$1.00, a $0.50 contango, +$7.00, a $1.00 contango, and now a $1.00 contango again - four of nine August sessions in contango and the front end has not held a premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August. THE HONEST READ: nothing about the physical front end changed today. The market repriced its expectations, not its prompt requirement. PROPORTION: $1.00 is 0.03% of cash and is effectively FLAT - the correct words remain 'no prompt premium', not 'prompt surplus'. avg = the July-2026 mean cash-3M spread of +$6.48 across the 23 published July sessions, so today sits $7.48 BELOW the July norm, exactly as it did yesterday.

lme.commentary: THE 12-AUGUST SESSION IS THE FIRST GENUINE TEST THIS RALLY HAS FAILED, AND THE WAY IT FAILED IS MORE USEFUL THAN THE FACT THAT IT DID. Cash settled $3,307.50 and the three-month $3,308.50, both down $65.50 (-1.94%) - the largest single-session decline of the August advance, arriving one ring after the published wave-(v) equality objective of $3,373 was met at $3,374.00. THE IDENTICAL DOLLAR MOVE IN BOTH LEGS IS THE DETAIL THAT CARRIES THE INFORMATION. Because cash and the three-month fell by exactly the same amount, the cash-3M spread is unchanged at a $1.00 contango and the front of the curve shifted DOWN IN PARALLEL. Parallel shifts are what happen when length leaves; they are not what happens when prompt physical need changes, because a change in prompt need necessarily moves the near leg more than the far one. For a week this desk has argued that a rally making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium was expectation-led rather than physical. Today the same logic runs in reverse and reaches the same place: the selling was not prompt either. NOTHING ABOUT THE PHYSICAL FRONT END CHANGED TODAY - EXPECTATIONS REPRICED. THREE FACTS CUT AGAINST READING THIS AS THE START OF A BREAK. First, stock drew AGAIN, 1,700 t to 251,700 t, a 31st consecutive session and a LARGER draw than the 1,500 t/day that had become routine - the price fell while the metal on warrant got scarcer. Second, aluminium fell essentially alone: zinc rose 1.04%, lead 0.63% and nickel 0.59%, and copper was flat, so a complex-wide risk event is not available as an explanation. Third, the macro backdrop was supportive rather than hostile - US July CPI printed 3.4% headline and 2.5% core, both easing - which is why the rest of the board rose. A metal that falls 2% into a supportive macro print, a tightening inventory and a stable curve is being sold by people who owned it, not by people who need less of it. THE PROPORTION, STATED PLAINLY SO THE MOVE IS NOT OVER-READ: cash remains $111.50 (+3.49%) above the 31-July official and $148.00 (+4.68%) above the 28-July swing low. This is a dent in momentum, not a change in trend. THE CLEAN TEST IS TOMORROW'S RING AND IT IS SPECIFIC: a second consecutive decline accompanied by a WIDENING contango would be the first hard evidence that the physical market is loosening rather than just the financial one. A second decline with the spread still pinned near flat would confirm today's read - position unwinding into an unchanged physical balance.

drivers.text: The front end did not firm on the sell-off, which leaves the prompt-tightness case exactly where it was — The 12-August official put cash at $3,307.50 against a three-month of $3,308.50 - a $1.00 CONTANGO, IDENTICAL to 11-August, because both legs fell by exactly $65.50. This is the single most important premium-relevant fact today and it is a fact about what did NOT happen. A physical market that was short of prompt metal would have seen the near leg fall less than the far one on a broad sell-off; instead the whole front of the curve shifted down in parallel. Four of nine August sessions have now closed in contango and the front end has not held a premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August. For a Q4 premium negotiation opening in late August, that record is the buyers' strongest evidence, and it is public and verifiable rather than anecdotal.

A 31st consecutive stock draw arrived on the day price fell 2%, and the draw accelerated — LME aluminium stock fell 1,700 t to 251,700 t on 12-August, a fresh cycle low and a LARGER withdrawal than the 1,500 t/day that ran for six of the seven preceding sessions. Visible inventory is down 23,475 t (-8.53%) across the fifteen sessions on this page and roughly half since January, with SMM describing levels near 250,000 t as the lowest since November 1990. This is the sellers' strongest public evidence and it cuts directly against the curve argument above: metal is leaving the exchange system even as the paper price falls. A premium is paid to obtain physical units in a region, so a shrinking global warrant pool is structurally supportive of premiums regardless of what the flat price does on any one day.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME aluminium stock series, 12-Aug-2026 session

drivers.text: A 6.3 Mt/y alumina refinery is entering a second day at half rate, and the cost is now quantified in dollars — Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - the largest alumina refinery outside China - cut production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA, part of New Fortress Energy, notified disruptions to natural gas availability. The company guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million from lost production and from purchasing gas above the contract price, is buying spot gas and has requested direct access to the Barcarena LNG terminal, and gives NO restart date beyond 'as soon as gas availability normalizes'. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina is off the seaborne balance. Alumina is not a premium, but a sustained alumina cost shock raises the marginal cost of every tonne of metal and historically leads regional premiums rather than following them.
drivers.source: AL Circle - Alunorte cuts alumina output to 50% as gas disruption threatens up to $100 million Q3 hit (11-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese physical buyers are visibly resisting the price level, which caps the demand-pull argument — SMM's 12-August coverage describes the South China spot market facing 'three mountains', with high absolute prices combined with high premiums prompting suppliers to rush to sell and cash out, while a companion note headlines SHFE aluminium stabilising at highs with destocking supporting a narrowing discount. SHFE aluminium rose 0.93% and the most-traded alumina contract rose 0.93% on the same session. THE COMBINATION IS THE SIGNAL: Chinese futures are following the rally while Chinese physical buyers are resisting it. Trading Economics reaches the same conclusion from the other side, noting futures remain below this year's four-year peaks on softening Chinese demand. Premium negotiations conducted against visibly reluctant Asian physical buying are harder for sellers to win.
drivers.source: SMM - SHFE Aluminum Stabilizes at Highs, Inventory Destocking Supports Discount Narrowing (12-Aug-2026)

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE ALUNORTE DISCLOSURE HAS BEEN FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, SO NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED FOR A SECOND RUN - the event is recorded, the price is not invented. The next public transaction print is the datapoint that converts the Alunorte headline into a cost fact, and it has not arrived. THE SUPPLY EVENT, RESTATED BECAUSE IT IS STILL THE DOMINANT ALUMINA FACT: Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - reduced production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability, and guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million while calling the full impact uncertain. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina is off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a $9/mt rally. The honest read on the two together is that the seaborne market held around the mid-$350s FOB through the first week of August. MARGIN CONTEXT AT TODAY'S LOWER METAL PRICE, AND THE RATIO MOVED AGAINST SMELTERS TODAY: against the 12-August three-month official of $3,308.50 the FOB mark now sits at about 10.8% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 11.0%, up from 10.6% and 10.8% yesterday purely because metal fell. Both remain well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%, so the alumina leg is still a TAILWIND to smelter economics - but the tailwind narrows mechanically every time metal falls, and Alunorte remains the first credible threat to it this year.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply goes to half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way. A LIVE MARKET SIGNAL THIS RUN: the most-traded SHFE alumina contract rose 0.93% on 12-August, the same session LME aluminium fell 1.94% - the Chinese alumina complex is not following the metal down.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review. THE NEXT EDITION IS DUE TODAY on the publication's Thursday cadence and had not printed at this 03:40 London compile, so the row is carried rather than marked. SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION FROM THE 11-AUGUST COST REVIEW: imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT CARRIED FROM LAST RUN: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders; CEO Patrice L'Huillier named Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

headlines.title: THE RALLY BROKE, AND IT BROKE ONE SESSION AFTER THE TARGET WAS MET. The 12-August LME official put cash at $3,307.50, down $65.50 (-1.94%) from $3,373.00, and the three-month at $3,308.50, down the same $65.50. It is the largest single-session decline of the entire August advance and it ends a run of five new cycle highs in eight sessions. The sequence is textbook: this page carried a wave-(v) equality objective of $3,373 for a week, the 11-August official printed $3,374.00 and met it to within $1.00, and the very next ring gave back $65.50. That does not prove the count was right, but it is exactly what the count said would happen. The 1.618x extension at $3,392 was never reached. Proportion matters in both directions: cash is still $111.50 (+3.49%) above the 31-July official of $3,196.00 and $148.00 (+4.68%) above the 28-July swing low. Momentum broke; the trend has not.

THE CURVE DID NOT CRACK - AND THAT IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE FACT ON THE PAGE. Cash and the three-month fell by EXACTLY the same $65.50, so the cash-3M spread is unchanged at a $1.00 CONTANGO, identical to yesterday. A perfectly parallel shift of the front of the curve is the signature of length leaving the market, not of any change in prompt physical requirement: a genuine demand shock or a squeeze unwinding moves one leg more than the other. Note the inversion of the week's message. While price was climbing, the front end kept giving up its premium, which said the buying was forward-dated rather than prompt. Today price fell 1.94% and the front end did not loosen at all, which says the selling was not prompt either. Four of nine August sessions have now closed in contango and the front end has not held a premium two sessions running since 04-August.

A 31ST CONSECUTIVE DRAW - AND THE DRAW ACCELERATED ON THE DAY THE PRICE FELL. LME aluminium stock fell 1,700 t to 251,700 t on 12-August, a fresh cycle low, and the withdrawal was LARGER than the 1,500 t/day that had run for six of the seven preceding sessions. Across the fifteen sessions on this page stock has fallen 23,475 t (-8.53%) from 275,175 t on 23-July, and roughly half since January. THE DIVERGENCE IS THE POINT: visible metal got scarcer on a day the price fell nearly 2%. SMM's 12-August wire describes LME warehouse inventories near 250,000 t as the LOWEST SINCE NOVEMBER 1990, a better-sourced and longer-dated framing than the 'lowest this century' wording used earlier and the one adopted here. A price falling into a tightening inventory is not a stable configuration; one side eventually gives.

DAY TWO AT HALF RATE FOR THE LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA, AND STILL NO RESTART DATE. Norsk Hydro disclosed at 07:01 CEST on 11-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para, Brazil - 6.3 million tonnes a year of nameplate alumina capacity - reduced production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA, part of New Fortress Energy, notified disruptions to natural gas availability. Contingency measures are the purchase of spot gas volumes and a request for direct access to the Barcarena LNG receiving and regasification terminal; the company says it will ramp back to full production 'as soon as gas availability normalizes' and will pursue long-term alternative gas supply while preserving its rights under the Gas Supply Agreement. THE FINANCIAL GUIDANCE IS THE PART THAT MAKES THIS CONCRETE: a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million from lost production plus buying gas above the contract price. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina is off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period. No public seaborne alumina price print dated after the disclosure was found at this compile, so no alumina value on this dashboard has been changed - the event is recorded, the price is not invented.

ALUMINIUM FELL ALONE, WHICH ARGUES THE MOVE WAS METAL-SPECIFIC RATHER THAN MACRO. On the 12-August three-month official zinc rose +1.04%, lead +0.63% and nickel +0.59%, copper was essentially unchanged at -0.11%, and aluminium fell -1.94%. Two sessions earlier aluminium had led the complex higher; it gave the entire lead back on its own. A broad risk-off event would have dragged the other four metals down with it and did not. THE STRUCTURAL PICTURE INVERTED TOO: copper's cash-over-three-month backwardation NARROWED from $207.50 to $175.00 and zinc's from $81.00 to $72.00, while nickel's contango widened from $200.00 to $215.00 and lead's from $29.00 to $39.00 - the whole complex loosened at the front end EXCEPT aluminium, whose spread did not move at all. Copper cash settled $14,376.00 and copper stock drew a further 2,425 t to 212,125 t.

US JULY CPI CAME IN SOFT ON THE SAME DAY ALUMINIUM FELL 2%, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT THAT THE TWO ARE UNRELATED. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on 12-August that headline CPI rose 0.1% month-on-month and 3.4% over the twelve months to July, easing from 3.5% in June, with core CPI up 0.2% on the month and 2.5% year-on-year, down a tenth. Shelter accounted for roughly two-thirds of the headline increase. A softer inflation print is, other things equal, supportive for industrial metals - it lowers the pressure on real rates and on the cost of carrying commodity length - and the rest of the base complex behaved accordingly, with three of five metals higher. Aluminium did the opposite. When a metal falls 2% against a macro backdrop that supported its peers, the explanation is usually inside that metal's own positioning, not outside it. US PPI is the next scheduled print.

IRAN RESTATED THAT HORMUZ STAYS CLOSED, AND THE US ENERGY AGENCY RAISED ITS OIL FORECAST ON THAT ASSUMPTION. Iran's state broadcaster IRIB, citing an advisor to the Supreme Leader, reported on 11-August that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until relevant conditions are met. Separately the US Energy Information Administration's latest Short-Term Energy Outlook raised its 2026 Brent forecast to an average $87/bbl from $82/bbl, explicitly assuming that severe shipping restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz persist into August, and expects some supply disruption of around 600,000 b/d to persist until end-2027. THE RELEVANCE TO THIS PAGE IS DIRECT AND RUNS THROUGH TWO CHANNELS: the Gulf accounted for roughly a tenth of global primary aluminium production before the conflict and its export routes remain impaired, and higher crude feeds green petroleum coke and therefore the calcined coke and prebaked anode legs of the smelter cost basket. Iran's oil ministry separately said on 11-August that damaged gas processing facilities should restore pre-war capacity of 95 million cubic metres a day by end-September.

CHINESE SPOT DEMAND IS VISIBLY STRUGGLING WITH THE PRICE LEVEL, WHICH IS THE CLEAREST DEMAND-SIDE WARNING ON THIS PAGE. SMM's 12-August coverage describes the South China spot market facing 'three mountains', with high absolute prices combined with high premiums prompting suppliers to rush to sell and cash out, and a separate SMM note the same day headlined SHFE aluminium stabilising at highs with inventory destocking supporting a narrowing discount. SHFE aluminium itself rose 0.93% and the most-traded alumina contract rose 0.93% on 12-August. THE HONEST READ OF THE COMBINATION: Chinese futures are following the rally while Chinese physical buyers are resisting it - the classic late-stage configuration in which a price is held up by paper rather than by consumption. Trading Economics' own summary of the market makes the same point from the other direction, noting futures remain below this year's four-year peaks on softening Chinese demand.

THE COST FLOOR KEEPS RISING FROM TWO INDEPENDENT DIRECTIONS AND NEITHER HAS REVERSED. SMM's 11-August cost review put China's national weighted-average FULL alumina production cost at RMB 2,718/mt in July, up RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with weighted-average cash cost at RMB 2,544/mt, and guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore - with caustic soda regionally divergent (Shanxi contracts expected up RMB 50/mt in August, Guangxi down RMB 150/mt) and energy slightly lower. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for purely domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne alumina supply has gone to half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way. The next scheduled hard datapoint is the SMM Bauxite Weekly Review, whose cadence is Thursday - due today.

A PUBLISHED TARGET WAS MET, THEN THE MARKET REVERSED - AND AN INDEPENDENT PRICE SERIES AGREES ON THE MAGNITUDE. Trading Economics' independent CFD series marks aluminium at $3,306.75 for 12-August, down 1.60% on the day against a prior mark of $3,360.55, while still up 4.79% on the month and 26.66% year-on-year. That an unrelated series agrees on both the direction and roughly the size of a 2% down day matters more on a reversal session than on a quiet one, because it rules out a single-source artefact. The technical read is that the wave-(v) equality objective at $3,373 was met at $3,374.00 on 11-August and the next objective, the 1.618x extension at $3,392, was never reached before the reversal. A target met and immediately rejected is the most common way an impulse terminates. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, STATED FAIRLY: one down day after eight up sessions proves nothing on its own, and the count only becomes materially safer if a second consecutive decline arrives with a WIDENING contango rather than a flat one.

The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. status.update: DISCLOSED 11-AUG-2026 AT 07:01 CEST UNDER SECTION 5-12 OF THE NORWEGIAN SECURITIES TRADING ACT AND UNCHANGED AT THIS COMPILE - NO FOLLOW-UP DISCLOSURE, NO RESTART DATE, SECOND DAY AT HALF RATE. Alunorte in Barcarena, Para, Brazil - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - reduced production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA, part of New Fortress Energy, notified disruptions to natural gas availability. Contingency measures are the purchase of spot gas volumes and a request for direct access to the Barcarena LNG receiving and regasification terminal. The company guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina financial impact of US$75-100 million from reduced production and above-contract gas purchases, while calling the full impact uncertain, and says it will ramp back up 'as soon as gas availability normalizes' while pursuing long-term alternative gas supply and preserving its rights under the Gas Supply Agreement. CONTEXT THAT MAKES THIS A PATTERN RATHER THAN AN INCIDENT: the same group has already declared force majeure on aluminium sales twice this year, the first after its Qatalum joint venture in Qatar was forced to cut production on natural gas shortages following damage to Middle East energy infrastructure, the second after Qatalum terminated a long-standing marketing agreement. Three gas-driven production events across two continents in one year - gas AVAILABILITY, not gas price, is the binding constraint.

catalysts.text: THE 13-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL, AND SPECIFICALLY WHETHER THE CONTANGO WIDENS ON A SECOND DOWN DAY. This is by some distance the highest-information event on the calendar and the test is precise. A SECOND CONSECUTIVE DECLINE WITH A WIDENING CONTANGO would be the first hard evidence that the physical market is loosening rather than just the financial one, and would put the 05-August wave (iv) low at $3,229.50 in play. A SECOND DECLINE WITH THE SPREAD STILL PINNED NEAR FLAT confirms today's read - position unwinding into an unchanged physical balance - and is the least informative outcome. A FIRM RING WITH THE FRONT END REBUILDING INTO BACKWARDATION while stock keeps drawing would say the flush cleared froth out of a genuinely tight market and would re-expose $3,374.00 and the untouched 1.618x extension at $3,392. Watch the stock line alongside: a 32nd consecutive draw on a second down day would sharpen the divergence further.

risks.text: POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG - THE RISK THAT PARTLY DISCHARGED TODAY. This desk has argued for a week that a rally making new highs while the front end surrendered its premium was carried by expectation rather than prompt need. On 12-August $65.50 came out of the price in a single session, one ring after a published technical target was met to within $1.00, and it came out in a perfectly parallel curve shift - the fingerprint of length leaving. THE TREND IS SET TO DOWN DELIBERATELY AND FOR A STATED REASON: some of this risk has now been realised rather than merely identified, so the residual exposure is lower today than it was at $3,374.00. It is NOT eliminated - the structural condition that created it, a front end that will not hold a premium, is entirely unchanged.

ALUNORTE GAS DISRUPTION EXTENDS AND BECOMES AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK. Day two at 50 percent with no restart date, no follow-up disclosure, and a company-guided potential Q3-2026 impact of US$75-100 million. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised seaborne alumina is out. The supplier issue is gas AVAILABILITY rather than price, which is harder to solve quickly than a commercial dispute, and the contingency measures announced - spot gas purchases and a request for direct LNG terminal access - are themselves evidence that the contracted route is not working. TREND UP: a second day without resolution makes an extended outage more likely than it was at disclosure, and no public alumina price print has yet arrived to size the market impact.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED - NOW WITH TWO INDEPENDENT SOURCES POINTING THE SAME WAY. Iran's state broadcaster restated on 11-August that the Strait remains closed until conditions are met, and the US EIA's latest Short-Term Energy Outlook raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $87/bbl explicitly assuming severe restrictions persist into August, with roughly 600,000 b/d of disruption lasting to end-2027. The Gulf was around a tenth of global primary production pre-conflict. This is the largest structural support under the price and simultaneously the largest single-headline downside risk if it reverses. TREND FLAT: the position hardened rhetorically but did not change in substance.

NEW SUPPLY ARRIVES ON SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY. The returning capacity is dated and identifiable: Slovalco 75,000 t/y in Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals about 75,000 t/y at New Madrid before year-end, Mt. Holly already at full capacity for the first time since 2015, continued cell-by-cell restoration at EGA's Al Taweelah, and Indonesian capacity advancing on schedule. SMM's July statistics already show outside-China daily average output UP 1.6% month-on-month even as the year-on-year total fell 6.7%. TREND UP: the marginal supply signal is improving month-on-month, which is the direction that hurts a supply-led rally.

THE STOCK DRAW STOPS OR REVERSES AND REMOVES THE BULL CASE'S BEST EVIDENCE. Six weeks of consecutive draws are the single strongest public argument for tightness, and the argument dies the day metal starts returning to warrant. TREND DOWN: today provided evidence AGAINST this risk rather than for it - the draw not only continued for a 31st session but ACCELERATED to 1,700 t from the 1,500 t/day that had become routine, and it did so on a 2% down day, which is precisely when a financially-motivated draw would be expected to pause.

MACRO TIGHTENING RAISES THE COST OF CARRYING COMMODITY LENGTH. Industrial metals are positioning-sensitive and long-dated financing costs bite hardest exactly when a rally is carried by financial rather than consumer demand - which is what this one has looked like. TREND DOWN: the macro pressure eased this run rather than building. US July CPI printed 3.4% headline and 2.5% core, both lower than June, the ten-year yield ticked down to 4.685% and the dollar index was flat at 99.94. Note the awkward implication for the bull case, stated honestly: aluminium fell 1.94% anyway, so easier financial conditions did not hold it up.

CHINESE PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. SMM's 12-August coverage describes the South China spot market facing 'three mountains', with high absolute prices and high premiums prompting suppliers to rush to sell and cash out; Trading Economics separately attributes futures remaining below this year's four-year peaks to softening Chinese demand. China is roughly 60% of global output and the marginal consumer of most seaborne units.
